title: week 6
introduction: This week, we explored the history of animation and its relationship with cinema, technology and human perception.We looked at how animation creates movement, transforms images and brings characters to life.For this week's assignment, I decided to create a short animation exploring how sound and image can contradict each other.
related_work: We explored Fantasmagorie (1908) by Émile Cohl, which uses simple drawings that continuously transform into different shapes.I was also interested in Duck Amuck (1953) by Chuck Jones, where the character's appearance, sounds and surroundings are repeatedly manipulated by an unseen animator.This work became the main inspiration for my animation.
method: Inspired by Duck Amuck, I developed a short animation about a character whose voice is unexpectedly changed.I used Procreate to draw a purple character in different poses and expressions, including waving, surprise, confusion and anger.I plan to arrange these drawings into a sequence and add mismatched sound effects and text.
results_discussion: Before this lecture, I mainly understood animation as a series of images creating the illusion of movement.However, the examples discussed in class encouraged me to pay more attention to how animation can use transformation and exaggeration as forms of expression.I was particularly interested in Fantasmagorie, where simple drawings continuously transform into different objects and shapes without following a conventional storyline.I found it interesting how these transformations could keep the audience engaged without realistic movements or detailed visuals.Another important example for me was Duck Amuck.Rather than simply telling a story, it reveals how the character is controlled by the animator, who can change its appearance, background and sounds.I particularly liked how these unexpected changes created humour while also making the audience aware of the animation process itself.This inspired me to create a short animation featuring a small purple character.My idea is that the character tries to greet the audience, but an unexpected sound comes out instead of its normal voice.The character then reacts with surprise, confusion and anger, eventually holding up a sign to protest.I also plan to explore how the text on the sign could be changed by an unseen creator, creating another contradiction between the character's intentions and what the audience sees.So far, I have drawn several expressions and poses in Procreate and started organising them into an animation sequence.One challenge is making the movement between poses feel natural, as I have little experience with frame-by-frame animation.This process has helped me understand that even a simple animation requires decisions about timing, movement and how the audience interprets the character's actions.
conclusion_future_work: This week helped me think about animation as more than a technique for creating movement.I became particularly interested in how animation can deliberately break the audience's expectations through changes in sound, image and character behaviour.
